+## What
+
+**Cross-repository task.** The code is in `/Users/wballard/github/swissarmyhammer/FoundationModelsACPAgent`.

+`Tests/FoundationModelsACPAgentTests/CommandDispatchTests.swift` holds two `guard case` blocks inside test bodies:
+
+```swift

+    ...
+    return
+}

+
+The rule `code-hygiene/idioms-swift` `noGuardInTests` refuses a `guard` in a test. A `guard ... else { return }` makes the test end quietly and report a pass when the shape is wrong.
+
+These two blocks are older than card `^321e315`. That card found them but did not touch them, because they are not the cause that card names.
+
+Correct the cause in the whole file, not only the two lines.
+
+- [ ] Replace each `guard case ... else { return }` in a test body with a direct `#expect` or `try #require` that fails when the shape is wrong
+- [ ] Read the whole file for the same cause, and correct every instance
+
+## Acceptance Criteria
+- [ ] No `guard` in a test body of `CommandDispatchTests.swift`
+- [ ] `swift test --filter CommandDispatchTests` passes
+- [ ] No new build warning
+
+## Tests
+- [ ] `swift test --filter CommandDispatchTests`

+comments:
+- actor: claude-code
+  id: 01m2qxdj2texmt28gkn0weckde
+  text: |
+    Research and implementation notes.
+
+    **The shape of the data.** `RequestError.data` is `JSONValue?` (FoundationModelsACP `Core/JSONValue.swift`). `JSONValue` has no accessor for the object members, so a test must match the `.object` case to reach them.
+
+    **The correction.** One private static helper `objectFields(in:)` in `CommandDispatchTests.swift` turns a `JSONValue?` into `[String: JSONValue]?`. Each of the two test bodies now reads:
+
+    ```swift
+    let fields = try #require(
+        Self.objectFields(in: error.data),
+        "expected object data, got \(String(describing: error.data))")
+    ```
+
+    A wrong shape now fails the test. The helper holds the only `guard`, and a helper `guard` gives a value to its caller; it does not end a test. The file already had this pattern in `commandNames(in:)`.
+
+    **Proof that the new form can fail.** I made the production `RequestError.unknownCommand` build `data: .array([...])` instead of `.object([...])`, then ran the one test twice:
+
+    - new `try #require` form: `Test run with 1 test in 1 suite failed ... with 1 issue` — `Expectation failed: Self.objectFields(in: error.data)` at CommandDispatchTests.swift:138:30, exit code 1.
+    - `guard case .object(let fields) = try #require(error.data) else { return }`: `Test run with 1 test in 1 suite passed`, exit code 0.
+
+    The production change was then reverted; `git status` shows only the test file modified.
+
+    **Sweep of the whole ACPAgent test target.** 25 `guard` statements sit inside `@Test` function bodies. 14 of them have the same cause as this card — a bare `return` in the `else` branch, which ends the test. They are in SessionLifecycleTests (1), PromptTurnTests (4), CommandRegistryTests (2), InitializationTests (2), CancellationTests (1), and Integration/TierTwoTests (5). They are out of the scope of this card, so they are recorded as new card ^jv3nxd5. The rest are guards inside closures that give a value to the closure's caller, which is not this cause.
